description: A simple CLI tool to help you remember terminal commands

summary.one_liner: Zev is a small Python CLI that turns natural-language requests into terminal commands using an LLM backend such as OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, or Azure OpenAI.
summary.what_it_does: Zev takes a plain-English description of a task and returns a suggested terminal command, helping users recall or discover commands they don't remember. It can be run in an interactive mode by typing `zev`, or with a one-off query passed as an argument. Setup is handled by a `zev --setup` prompt that asks for the provider and API key or model settings. It supports OpenAI, Google Gemini, Ollama (for fully local use), and Azure OpenAI. The README says it attempts to flag dangerous generated commands, though not reliably. Clipboard copy and paste is supported, with platform-specific helper tools needed on Linux.
use_cases: Discover command-line tools for a task
Check disk usage or running processes
Run an LLM-backed command helper locally with Ollama
Use Azure OpenAI for command suggestions
how_to_run: zev 'show disk usage for current directory'
stack: LLM APIs (OpenAI, Google Gemini, Ollama, Azure OpenAI)
notable: Interactive mode and direct one-shot query mode
Multiple LLM provider support with re-runnable setup
Optional Azure dependencies installable as an extra
caveats: Generated commands come from LLMs and may be wrong; dangerous commands may not always be flagged
Requires an API key or account with a provider (OpenAI requires a subscription); Ollama needs a locally running model
Clipboard features on Linux may need xclip, xsel, or wl-clipboard installed
